passage: Sunday. Dhruvi followed me from my room to the balcony and all the way to the bathroom door. Then she touched my eraser collection and lined the erasers up wrong. I snapped, "Stop it, they're mine!" and her lip wobbled. She said, "I just want to be like you, Bhaiya." I felt bad, because it is annoying but also kind of sweet. So I made a plan. I told her the collection is mine and she can look but must ask before touching, and every day at five we will play a game together. She said okay and smiled 😊. Tomorrow I will see if it works. -- Yogesh

qa.q: What did Dhruvi touch and line up wrong?
qa.a: She touched Yogesh's eraser collection and lined the erasers up wrong.

qa.q: Why did Yogesh feel bad after snapping at Dhruvi?
qa.a: Yogesh felt guilty, because Dhruvi's lip wobbled and she said she just wanted to be like him, so he realised she looks up to him.

qa.q: What kind limit did Yogesh set with Dhruvi?
qa.a: He told her the collection is his and she must ask before touching, and promised a game together every day at five.

qa.q: How might Dhruvi feel about Yogesh's rule?
qa.a: She said okay and smiled, so she may be a little disappointed about the erasers but glad to have a regular time with her big brother.

grounding: An older sibling who is irritated by a clingy younger sister sets a kind limit and offers shared time.

passage:
Sami's little sister Hana followed him everywhere around their Helsinki flat. To his room. To the kitchen. Even to the door when he went to get the mail. She touched his model planes and put his books in the wrong order.
"Hana, stop!" he snapped. Her face crumpled.
Sami sighed. He remembered following his cousin around the same way when he was little.
He knelt down. "Hana, my planes are mine. You can't touch them. But at five o'clock, we can play with your blocks together. Deal?"
Hana nodded. At five she was waiting on the floor with her blocks lined up.

qa.q: What did Hana touch in Sami's room?
How did Sami feel about Hana following him?
qa.a: He felt irritated, but also remembered following his cousin when he was little.

qa.q: What kind limit did Sami set?
qa.a: He told Hana his planes were his and not to be touched, but promised to play blocks with her at five.

qa.q: How might Hana feel about the five o'clock plan?
qa.a: Hana was clearly excited, waiting on the floor with her blocks lined up.

grounding: A boy's little sister follows him and touches his things; he feels irritated but sets a kind limit and promises to play with her later.

passage:
Every Saturday, Payal had swimming practice at the sports club, and her little sister Arohi came along with Papa. Arohi followed Payal to the lockers, to the shower, even to the pool edge, and touched her goggles and cap.
"Arohi, stop! These are mine!" Payal snapped. Arohi's eyes filled.
Payal took a breath. Arohi was only six and thought Payal was the best swimmer in the world.
"Okay. My goggles and cap are mine. But after practice, I'll teach you how to blow bubbles in the kids' pool."
Arohi's face lit up. She sat with Papa and watched every lap.

qa.q: What did Arohi touch at the pool edge?
How did Payal feel about Arohi following her?
qa.a: She felt irritated, but also knew Arohi admired her as the best swimmer in the world.

qa.q: What kind limit did Payal set?
qa.a: She said her goggles and cap were hers, but promised to teach Arohi to blow bubbles after practice.

qa.q: How might Arohi see her big sister?
qa.a: Arohi sees Payal as a hero, watching every lap from the side.

grounding: An older girl whose little sister follows her and touches her things sets a kind limit and promises to play together later.
